metadata.note: The Coal and Coke Railway (Elkins - Charleston, WV; Henry Gassaway Davis, incorporated 1902, through passenger service from 21 Jan 1906), its B&O-era successor service, and three predecessors: the Charleston, Clendennin and Sutton (Charleston - Clay), the Roaring Creek and Belington (Belington - Leiter Jct) and the Roaring Creek and Charleston (Norton - Coalton - Mabie). Drawn from research/branches/coal_and_coke_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains) (2026-10-26). Before this layer the map drew none of this corridor. Only the report's drawable spans are drawn, which keep to years a source confirms; the 1916-1924 gap between the C&C and B&O eras is deliberately left undrawn. Rule 4 split: independent C&C to 1917/1918 (a New York syndicate, not the B&O, bought control in Feb 1917), B&O control by 1918 (USRA, 1 July 1918; 1918 federal compensation), outright purchase 1933/1934. Elkins - Norton (6.9 mi) was WVC&P / Western Maryland track used jointly; the C&C and B&O features draw it on their own geometry in their own colour, and the WM feature in west_virginia_central_pittsburg.geojson is untouched. Mileposts are Fowler's, from Elkins.

not_yet_sourced: End years that are the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end ([OPEN]): Coal and Coke Elkins - Charleston 1915; B&O Adrian Jct - Orlando Jct 1951 (Grafton - Richwood trains 135/136 still running 30 Sept 1951, end not found); CC&S Charleston - Clay 1896.
Start years that are the first CONFIRMED year, not the start of service ([OPEN]): B&O Adrian Jct - Orlando Jct 1925, Orlando Jct - Gassaway 1925, Gassaway - Charleston 1920.
[ANCHOR] single proven years: B&O Elkins - Adrian Jct 1925 (ceiling 1941 abandonment), Sutton Branch 1925, RC&B Belington - Leiter Jct 1905, RC&C Norton - Mabie 1902.

B&O takeover date and nature (lease or stock control; 1917 or 1918) - the ICC valuation report and B&O annual reports for 1917-1918 should settle it. The C&C stayed separately operated to 1933/1934 and the June 1920 Guide still named it 'Coal & Coke R.R.'; if B&O control was stock-only the colour split should move to the date the B&O actually ran the trains (no later than 1925). Drawn years do not change either way.
C&C passenger service 1916-1917 and B&O-era service 1918-1924: almost certain, not confirmed by a dated source.
Gassaway passenger end: 'during 1951' (wvncrails, agreeing with the Feb 1952 Guide daggers) versus 'until 1953' (wvexplorer / theclio). 1951 used.
Whether the Grafton - Richwood train ran over Orlando Jct - Burnsville (Table 38 lists Burnsville undaggered).
Operator of the Belington - Leiter and Norton - Mabie passenger service (RC&B / RC&C or the C&C).
CC&S: opening of Charleston - Clendenin (1893?), C&C takeover date (1902 or c.1904), any service to Ivydale and the 1902-1905 railheads.
branches_deliberately_omitted: [6] B&O Gassaway - Charleston local / Elk River trains: no separate service found; covered by the Gassaway - Charleston feature.

[8] CC&S / C&C Clay - Ivydale and the 1902-1905 railheads: no confirmable passenger year (Official Guide station-list entries only, and the 1900 Ivydale extension is via a search summary). Omitted until sourced.
freight_only_excluded: Belington - Leiter Jct - Norton under the B&O (Feb 1952 Guide Table 93 'Freight service only').
Burnsville Junction - Gassaway - Charleston after 1951 (freight to ~1976, refinery traffic to 1983, Conrail Charleston - Hartland from 1985).
Midvale - Leiter Jct - Norton 1941-1972, freight only after the through route was cut.
Elk River Railroad 1996-2022 (freight and car storage; no excursion service found).
C&C coal and mine spurs (Shelley Junction, Loop, Laurel and others).

segments.note: First through passenger train Elkins - Charleston 21 January 1906 (e-WV; WV Public Broadcasting); last spike at Walkersville 2 Dec 1905 (e-WV; american-rails gives 1 Dec 1904 / 1 Dec 1905 - conflict recorded, it does not move the passenger start). Dated passenger evidence in Fowler's station list: 1906 C&C public timetable (Jessica, Swandale, Jacksonville), 1906 Official Guide (Gerwig, Nixon), 1909 Guide (Rouzer), 1911 Guide (Paddy Creek, Wirebridge), 1915 C&C public timetable (Halbert). [OPEN] Passenger service confirmed to 1915 by the 1915 C&C public timetable cited by Fowler. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: service very likely ran on until the B&O took control (1917/1918), but 1916-1917 is not proven. Do not extend without evidence, and do not widen it to meet the B&O features. Includes Elkins - Norton (6.9 mi), which was WVC&P / Western Maryland track the C&C used jointly; drawn here in C&C colour because the C&C ran these trains. Headway is an estimate (a pair of through trains assumed) and is NOT sourced.

segments.note: Ex-C&C east end under the B&O, Elkins (via WM joint track to Norton) - Norton - Leiter Jct - Kingsville - Midvale - Sago - Adrian Junction. wvncrails Part III reproduces 'a pair of 1925 B&O passenger timetables' with 'Two daily scheduled through trains and a Sunday only operated in both directions', and notes 'this is an Elkins Sub timetable which also includes Western Maryland trains at that endpoint'. [ANCHOR] 1925 is the single proven passenger year. Service certainly ran wider both ways (from B&O control in 1917/1918, and up to the cut), but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen this to look plausible. The ICC authorised abandonment of Midvale - Adrian Jct ('12 miles') on 27 Feb 1941 (Evening Star), which 'severed through service to Elkins' (american-rails): 1941 is an ABANDONMENT CEILING, not a passenger end year, and passengers may have stopped earlier. Afterwards Midvale - Leiter Jct - Norton stayed as freight to 1972, and the Feb 1952 Guide Table 93 (Belington Branch, Tygart Jct - Belington - Norton - Elkins) is 'Freight service only'. Headway from the 1925 timetable description (two daily through trains each way); avg_speed_kmh is an estimate.

segments.note: Orlando Junction - Burnsville - Gilmer - Gassaway, under the B&O. This feature also carries the 2.8 mi Orlando Jct - Burnsville stretch (Fowler mp 58.0 - 60.8), which the report places in its Burnsville - Gassaway - Charleston block ([4], 116.9 mi from mp 58.0); it is what connects the Adrian Jct - Orlando Jct feature to this one. segments.note: Gassaway - Frametown - Clay - Dundon - Clendenin - Charleston, under the B&O (control 1917/1918). [OPEN] start: 1920 is the first CONFIRMED B&O-era year - the Official Guide card of 16 June 1920 for the Buffalo Creek & Gauley reads 'Connection with the Coal & Coke R.R. at Dundon' (hawkinsrails) - not the start of service; 1918-1919 is unproven. 1925: 'Four eastbound (north) B&O trains and four westbound (south) counterparts' (wvncrails Part III). Mid-1950 'two passenger trains' Charleston - Gassaway, and train 136 left Charleston in the November 1950 Thanksgiving blizzard (wvncrails Part II). End 1951: 'B&O abolished its last passenger train on the line during 1951' (wvncrails Part I), agreeing with the primary Feb 1952 Guide (schedules of 30 Sept 1951), whose index daggers Gassaway, Frametown, Clay, Clendennin, Queen Shoals, Strange Creek and Villa Nova 'for freight service only' and whose Table 39 prints 'Freight Service'. CONFLICT recorded, not used: wvexplorer and theclio say the Gassaway depot served passengers 'until 1953'. CAVEAT on colour: the June 1920 Guide still called the road 'Coal & Coke R.R.' and the C&C stayed a separately operated B&O subsidiary to 1933/1934; drawn in B&O colour per the report's split at 1917/1918. Freight continued: through B&O freight to about 1976, Elk Refinery traffic to 1983, Conrail Charleston - Hartland from 1985. The NYC's Charleston - Blue Creek service is a different road. Headway from the 1925 count of four trains each way; avg_speed_kmh is an estimate.

Where the original alignment has been lifted and a successor line survives on the same corridor, the trace follows the surviving track, so short stretches may draw a LATER alignment than the era shown; no specific realignment on this road was identified.

segments.note: Gassaway - Bison - West Sutton - Sutton. wvncrails: 'the primary reason for the construction of the Sutton Branch was for additional passenger traffic directly serving Sutton', and it reproduces 'A 1925 timetable of the Sutton Branch near the zenith of passenger train travel' - 'A number of connecting trains operating between Sutton and Gassaway gives testimony to the volume of traffic'. [ANCHOR] 1925 is the single proven passenger year. The branch surely carried passengers both before and after 1925, but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen this to look plausible. No 1951 table for Sutton was found; the 1952 Guide index mark on 'Sutton, W. Va., B.& O' is mangled ('*' or freight-only dagger) and is not used as a date. The separate ex-WV&P Flatwoods - Sutton branch (abandoned 1931) is a different line. Abandoned mid-1980s. Headway is an estimate ('a number of connecting trains') and is NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced: 50.7 mi against the documented 50.9 mi (Fowler, 174.9 - 124.0). Same geometry as the Clay - Charleston part of the C&C feature: 50.8 mi on ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O or the OHM 'Coal and Coke Railroad' grade (24.1 mi OHM, Clendenin - Charleston), 0.1 mi trail. No straight-line leg longer than 300 m. Drawn on the C&C-era grade; any pre-1906 alignment the CC&S used that the C&C later rebuilt is not known and not drawn - this may be a LATER alignment than the 1895-1896 era.

segments.note: Charleston - Two Mile - Blue Creek - Clendenin - Queen Shoals - Elkhurst - Clay, the predecessor road. 1895: WV Explorer says 'the first passenger train that operated between Clay and Charleston was run in 1895'; Goldenseal (Fall 2016, quoted via search results only - not fetched) dates Clay's first train to 10 December 1895. 1896: Fowler records 1896 Official Guide names for Elkhurst, Shelton, Shelley Junction, Reamer and Milliken, so the CC&S had a passenger table in the 1896 Guide. [OPEN] 1896 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end; the CC&S era ends when the Davis interests took over operation c.1902-1904, and the 1897-1905 gap before the C&C feature is unproven, not a known suspension. Do not extend without evidence. Charleston - Clendenin may have opened earlier (WV Explorer's Clendenin page says 1893, unverified). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced: 7.8 mi against the documented 8.5 mi (Fowler table 12, 33.0 to 41.5). Composition: 4.9 mi on ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O (Valley River Road, West Junior Road and the abandoned grade south of Belington - the RC&B's own alignment on the west side of the Tygart Valley), 2.7 mi on untagged OpenHistoricalMap rail over two gaps in the B&O-tagged chain (about 1.2 mi south of Junior, and about 1.5 mi from West Junior into Leiter Jct), 0.2 mi connectors. CAUTION (Tygart Valley trap): those 2.7 OHM miles lie within 10-40 m of the parallel WVC&P / WM grade, so over them the feature may draw the WM's alignment rather than the RC&B's. A plain trace put the whole branch on the WM; it was re-run with every non-B&O way costed 4x and pinned through the B&O-tagged chain ends. No straight-line leg longer than 300 m. Starts at the B&O-tagged grade's end, 0.5 km from the Belington geocode.

segments.note: Belington - Wilson - Latham - West Junior - Island Run - Skidmore - Findlay - Leiter Junction, paralleling the WM. [ANCHOR] 1905 is the single proven passenger year, from Fowler's 'Findlay [Findley 1905G]' (an Official Guide timetable name). Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen this to look plausible. Fowler's table 12 header: 'Belington-Leiter ex Coal & Coke Rly, passenger service withdrawn before merger with BO' - which merger (1917/1918 control or 1933/1934 purchase) is not said. OPERATOR UNCERTAIN: the RC&B was a separate company owned by the Davis Colliery Co. until Feb 1917 (Belington Progressive), and is drawn under its own name and colour, but Fowler attributes the passenger service to the Coal & Coke, which may have worked it. Freight only under the B&O (Feb 1952 Guide Table 93). Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.

segments.note: Norton (Roaring Creek Junction) - Scotts Mill - Jeff Scotts - Phillips Mill - Coalton - Fisher - Mabie, in the Roaring Creek coalfield. [ANCHOR] 1902 is the single proven passenger year, from Fowler's 'Coalton [Womelsdorff 1902G]' (an Official Guide timetable name). Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed under any operator. Do not widen this to look plausible. OPERATOR UNCERTAIN: in 1902 probably the Roaring Creek & Charleston, which Davis bought that year; after 1906 a C&C branch off the main line at Norton. Freight only by its later B&O abandonment; the 1952 Guide's 'Coalton, W. Va., Balt.& O' index mark is mangled and not used as a date. Headway is an estimate and is NOT sourced.
